name: Buffalo Creek coal-waste slurry dam failure
location: Buffalo Creek hollow, Logan County, West Virginia
notes: Coal preparation (washery) refuse slurry; Pittston Coal. Volume 500,000 m3 (about 132 million US gal). Gross mass = volume x slurry density 1.15 t/m3 (judgement); solids fraction 0.25 (0.15-0.35, judgement) carries the activity. Activity modelled: coal-refuse coefficient 2.3e5 Bq/t (Ra-226 53, Th-232 61 Bq/kg, U-238 and Ra-228 assumed equal to their chain neighbours). Date exact. to_tiers liberated only because coal_mining does not allow dispersed (vocab); slurry flowed down the creek valley.

name: Three Mile Island Unit 2 partial core melt
notes: Offsite release 28 Mar-7 Apr 1979 (S0108 window). Noble gases (Xe-133 dominant, some Kr-85, Xe-133m, Xe-135): central 2.5 MCi (Rogovin, S0138 cited in the nuclear notes; NOT retrieved), NRC letter S0108 gives consultants about 10 MCi, one alternative 2.4 MCi, NRC range 1-40 MCi (used as low/high). I-131 about 14 Ci (5e11 Bq, negligible against noble gases, added to central). Spread of one order of magnitude or more. Damaged core stayed in TMI-2 vessel; fuel was later removed (spent-fuel handling is outside this event).

name: Church Rock uranium mill tailings spill (United Nuclear)
location: Church Rock, McKinley County, New Mexico (coordinates approximate)
notes: Acidic mill liquor (94 million US gal = 3.56e5 m3, taken at 1.0 t/m3) plus about 1,100 short tons solids. Central activity 46 Ci gross alpha read from a garbled table row in S0709 (columns: volume, pH, t U 1.5, U mg/L 4.5-6.4, Ra total 210 pCi/L, gross alpha 46 Ci) - consistent with a river gross-alpha peak of about 1.3e5 pCi/L in S0109 but the column assignment is NOT verified against the original slide; gross alpha includes progeny so it is not a head-activity sum. Low = natural U only (1.5 t U x 25.4 kBq/g); high = 3 x central (judgement). Passes mass criterion on its own; activity criterion met only if 46 Ci is right. Coordinates approximate. Civil (commercial mill).

name: Chernobyl Unit 4 (RBMK-1000) explosion and fire
notes: Release to atmosphere 26 Apr-6 May 1986. Central = sum of UNSCEAR 2008 Table 1 (S0105) nuclides in head activity, 1.206e19 Bq (Xe-133 6,500 PBq = 54 %). Low 1.09e19 = OECD-NEA table sum (S0710, omits I-133 and Te-129m, so a lower bound). High 1.29e19 = central with UNSCEAR 2000 (S0104) higher refractory values (Zr-95 196, Ce-141 196, Ce-144 116, Np-239 945 PBq; Ce-141 196 is also in the NEA table S0710, whose Np-239 value of about 95 is a typo for 3.5 % of 27,000 = 945). IAEA Bulletin 1996 (S0711) quotes about 12 EBq, consistent. Country coded SUN (valid to 1991); deposition mainly UKR, BLR, RUS. Quantity moved to sealed_damaged_core (shelter) is the unreleased remainder of the core and is a Phase 2 calculation from S0104 Table 1 inventories.

name: Maritsa Iztok-1 (Stara Zagora) ash-dam failure
location: Maritsa Iztok-1 power plant, near Stara Zagora
notes: Lignite ash and cinder; WISE lists 500,000 m3 for a dam failure from beach inundation (WISE gives 1 March 1992; day-level precision not independently confirmed). Mass and solids fraction are judgement (slurry 1.2 t/m3, 35 % solids); ash coefficient is the generic US value, probably low for Bulgarian lignite ash. Only one secondary source (WISE); primary not found.

name: Marcopper copper mine tailings spill (Marinduque)
notes: Commodity: COPPER. Tailings leaked from the Tapian pit storage through an old drainage tunnel; 1.6 million m3 (WISE). Density 1.5 t/m3 (1.2-1.8, judgement). Generic metal-tailings coefficient (2.8e5 Bq/t; range 8e4-9e5). Attribution to wind/solar by allocation rules (METHODS 10.2).

name: Los Frailes (Aznalcollar) pyrite tailings dam failure
notes: Commodity: ZINC / LEAD / COPPER / SILVER (Boliden Los Frailes). WISE: 4-5 million m3 toxic water and slurry. Gross mass at 1.2 t/m3; solids fraction 0.35 (judgement) carries the metal-tailings coefficient. Commodity split is a Task 2.x allocation problem; stage commodity_supply with product zinc/lead/silver/copper.

name: Tokaimura JCO fuel-fabrication criticality accident
notes: Civil fuel conversion plant (fuel for the Joyo experimental fast reactor), INES 4. WNA (S0708, grey): about 160 TBq noble gases and 2 TBq gaseous iodine apparently released. Low/high = central /10, x10 (judgement: single grey source, no primary release table found; NRC S0726 gives about 2.5e18 fissions but its text is garbled). Filed at the routine-transfer stage conv_enrich_fab as an EVENT transfer out of sealed_fuel_cycle (allowed by SCHEMA 3.1); the accident stage has no sealed_fuel_cycle tier. Release ended within about a day (end date not confirmed, left empty).

name: Martin County coal-slurry impoundment failure (Inez, Kentucky)
notes: Washery slurry (coal fines, silt, clay). Volume 300 million US gal (ATSDR; 1.14e6 m3), range 250 (WISE, 0.95e6 m3) to 306 million gal. Solids fraction 0.25 (judgement). Activity modelled with coal-refuse coefficient. Slurry discharged via mine workings into Wolf Creek / Coldwater Fork and the Tug Fork basin. Largest by volume of the listed slurry failures. Coordinates approximate.

name: Partizansk ash-dump ring-dike break (Dalenergo)
notes: MARGINAL on mass: about 160,000 m3 ash slurry; gross mass 1.9e5 t at 1.2 t/m3 (low case 1.6e5 t still above 1e5 t). Solids fraction 0.35 (judgement). Single secondary source (WISE). Generic ash coefficient.

name: TVA Kingston Fossil Plant fly-ash impoundment failure
notes: Ash volume 5.4 million cubic yards (4.13e6 m3). Density 1.36 t/m3 from EPA closeout: 3.5 million cy removed = 4.0 million short tons shipped (S0703); low 1.0 (dry), high 1.5 (judgement). Activity modelled: Ra-226 163 and Ra-228 115 Bq/kg (Ruhl 2009 TDEC means 4.4 and 3.1 pCi/g), U-238 and Th-232 assumed equal to their chain neighbours = 5.6e5 Bq/t, x0.5/x2. Ash entered Emory/Clinch Rivers (liberated) and about 120 ha of land (dispersed); split not published. Date exact. Pb-210/Po-210 enrichment not included.

name: Ajka (Kolontar) red-mud reservoir failure, MAL Zrt
notes: Commodity: ALUMINIUM (bauxite residue). 700,000 m3 caustic red-mud slurry (WISE). Gross at 1.25 t/m3, solids fraction 0.3 (judgement). Red-mud coefficient 9.8e5 Bq/t = Th-232 400 + Ra-226 300 + U-238 280 Bq/kg (ranges in S0409 Table 2, S0008). Fully civil. Coordinates approximate.

name: Fukushima Daiichi Units 1-3 core damage and releases
notes: Atmospheric release (UNSCEAR 2013 Table 2, S0106): Xe-133 7,300; I-131 120; Te-132 29; Cs-137 8.8; Cs-134 9.0; Cs-136 1.8; I-133 9.6 PBq (I-132 29 PBq omitted: it is a Te-132 daughter, counted in the Te132+ group). Direct ocean (S0107): Cs-137 3.5-5.6, I-131 9-13, H-3 0.3-0.7 PBq (midpoints used; Cs-134 ocean not given). Central 7.49e18. Low 7.3e18 = Xe-133 only (a lower bound). High 1.62e19 = Stohl 2012 (S0701) Xe-133 15.3 EBq, Cs-137 36.6 PBq, plus S0107 upper I-131 754 PBq and upper ocean values. Main atmospheric release 12-23 March 2011; ocean release continues at low level. Date_end is a convention.

name: Padcal (Philex) tailings pond no. 3 breach
notes: Commodity: COPPER (with gold). WISE reports 20.6 million t of tailings (a mass, not a volume), used directly: 2.06e7 t. Coordinates approximate. Generic metal-tailings coefficient.

name: Obed Mountain coal-mine wash-plant pond breach (Sherritt)
location: Obed Mountain Mine near Hinton, Alberta
notes: Coal preparation plant wastewater 670,000 m3 plus 90,000 t sediment (WISE). Gross mass 7.6e5 t (water at 1 t/m3); only the 90,000 t sediment carries activity (coal-refuse coefficient 2.3e5 Bq/t). Reached the Athabasca River system. Single secondary source.

name: Duke Energy Dan River Steam Station ash-pond release
notes: MARGINAL on mass: ash 39,000 short tons (35,400 t; revised from 82,000 short tons; WISE gives 74,400 t as high) plus 27 million US gal (1.02e5 m3, taken at 1 t/m3) of pond water = 1.38e5 t. Ash alone is below 1e5 t, so the event passes only if pond water counts as NORM-bearing material (flag for orchestrator). Activity counted on ash only (water ignored): ash coefficient 5.6e5 Bq/t; low = 30,000 short tons x 0.5, high = 74,400 t x 2. End date 2014-02-08 is when the pipe was sealed (WFAE: Saturday).

name: Mount Polley tailings storage facility breach (Imperial Metals)
notes: Commodity: COPPER (with gold). Tailings 7.3 million m3 (WISE) to 8 million m3 (BC Government, with 17 million m3 water); the free and interstitial water is not counted. Density 1.5 t/m3 (1.2-1.8). Generic metal-tailings coefficient; Mount Polley ore is a low-U porphyry. Coordinates approximate.

name: Fundao (Samarco) iron-ore tailings dam failure, Mariana
notes: Commodity: IRON ORE (steel). About 32 million m3 released (Samarco 60-day update, BHP); early estimates exceeded 50 million m3. Density 1.8 t/m3 (1.5-2.1). Generic metal-tailings coefficient, probably HIGH for itabirite iron ore (very low U/Th); the low bound (8e4 Bq/t) is more likely. Flowed to the Rio Doce and Atlantic.

name: Dahegou (Luoyang) red-mud tailings dam failure
notes: Commodity: ALUMINIUM (bauxite residue). WISE lists 2 million m3 for Luoyang Xiangjiang Wanji Aluminium; single secondary source and the material type (red mud vs other bauxite tailings) is as stated by WISE. Same red-mud coefficient and slurry assumptions as Ajka.

name: Cadia (Newcrest) tailings storage facility failure
notes: Commodity: COPPER (with gold). 1.33 million m3 of tailings (WISE), mostly retained on site. Density 1.5 t/m3 (1.2-1.8). Generic metal-tailings coefficient. Only part of the failed mass left the facility boundary; treated as all released (upper bound). Coordinates approximate.

name: Corrego do Feijao (Vale) dam B-I failure, Brumadinho
notes: Commodity: IRON ORE (steel). 9.7 million m3 released (ASDSO case study) to 12 million m3 (WISE). Density 1.8 t/m3 (1.5-2.1). Generic metal-tailings coefficient, probably HIGH for iron-ore tailings (see E018). Coordinates approximate.
